title: Why p99 latency matters
subtitle: Averages can hide the users having a terrible time
learning_objective: Interpret p50, p95, and p99 latency and understand why averages are insufficient.

scenes.title: AVERAGE LOOKS FINE
scenes.body: Average latency is 120 ms, but some users wait several seconds. The average hides the tail.

scenes.title: Percentiles describe the distribution
scenes.body: p50 is the median. p95 is the latency at or below which 95% of measured requests fall. p99 focuses on the slowest 1%.

scenes.title: Read the tail
items: Compare by endpoint and time window

scenes.title: Don't chase one number
scenes.body: Percentiles depend on sample size, aggregation method, and time window. Pair them with request volume, errors, and traces to diagnose causes.

scenes.question: If p99 latency is 2 seconds, what does that indicate?
options: About 99% of measured requests are at or below 2 seconds
scenes.explanation: p99 is a latency percentile, not an error rate; about 99% of observations are at or below that value under the chosen calculation.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Monitor percentiles to expose slow-tail behavior, then segment and investigate the affected requests.
